title: 21 — Design Ad Click Event Aggregation
html:
21 — Design Ad Click Event Aggregation

The one idea: billing depends on these numbers, so the design is about correctness under stream processing: aggregate click events per ad per minute using event time with watermarks for late data, get exactly-once effects through idempotent writes, and reconcile against raw data in a nightly batch job.

Step 1 — Scope

  • Input: log of click events (ad_id, click_timestamp, user_id, ip, country).
  • 1 billion clicks/day, 2M ads, 30% YoY growth.
  • Queries:
    1. Clicks for ad_id in the last M minutes.
    2. Top 100 most-clicked ads in the last minute (configurable window).
    3. Filter both by ip, user_id, country.
  • Late and duplicate events must be handled; results visible within minutes; correctness is critical (billing).

Estimates: 1B ÷ 10^5 ≈ 10,000 QPS average, peak ~50,000; ~0.1 KB per event → 100 GB/day raw.

Step 2 — High-level design

Two data kinds

Raw data Aggregated data
Full history ✅ ❌
Supports new queries / recompute ✅ ❌
Size Huge Small
Query speed Slow Fast

Store both: raw (write-heavy → Cassandra / data lake) as the source of truth; aggregates for queries.

---
title: Ad click aggregation — high-level architecture
---
flowchart LR
    Logs["Log watcher"] --> MQ1["Kafka: raw clicks"]
    MQ1 --> RawDB[("Raw data DB<br/>(cold, source of truth)")]
    MQ1 --> Agg["Aggregation service<br/>(stream: map → aggregate → reduce)"]
    Agg --> MQ2["Kafka: aggregated counts"]
    MQ2 --> AggDB[("Aggregation DB")]
    AggDB --> QS["Query service / dashboard"]
    RawDB --> Recon["Nightly batch<br/>reconciliation"]
    Recon --> AggDB

The second queue lets the aggregation service achieve end-to-end exactly-once (atomic commit of output + consumed offsets).

Aggregation as a DAG (MapReduce-style)

  • Map node: filter/clean, route by ad_id % n.
  • Aggregate node: count per ad_id per minute in memory.
  • Reduce node: merge partial results (e.g. top-100 heap from each aggregator → global top-100).

Data model

ad_click_count  (ad_id, click_minute, filter_id, count)
top_ads         (window_size, update_time_minute, most_clicked_ads[])
filter          (filter_id, region, ip, user_id)     -- star schema for filters

Step 3 — Deep dive

3.1 Streaming vs batch

Use streaming for freshness and batch for recomputation/reconciliation. That's the Lambda architecture (two code paths); Kappa uses one streaming path and replays the log for recomputation — simpler to maintain ✅.

3.2 Time

Event time (when clicked) Processing time (when processed)
Accuracy ✅ Correct Skewed by delays
Late events Must be handled Not an issue

Use event time + a watermark (extend the window by, say, 15 s to wait for stragglers). Very late events are corrected by reconciliation.

3.3 Windows

  • Tumbling (fixed, non-overlapping, 1 min) → clicks per ad per minute.
  • Sliding / hopping → top-100 in the last M minutes.

3.4 Delivery guarantees

Duplicates (client retries, consumer crashes before committing offset) would inflate bills.

  • Store the offset with the aggregated result atomically (transaction or idempotent upsert keyed by (ad_id, minute)), or use Kafka transactions for exactly-once processing.
  • Dedupe events by a click ID within a window.

3.5 Scaling

  • Kafka: partition by ad_id; enough partitions up front (changing breaks key→partition mapping).
  • Aggregation: add nodes; hotspot ads (viral) → allocate more aggregator nodes for that ad and merge.
  • Aggregation DB: write-heavy time-series-like → Cassandra / ClickHouse / Druid.

3.6 Fault tolerance

Aggregation state is in memory → snapshot state + offsets periodically; on failure, restore the snapshot and replay from the saved offset.

3.7 Data monitoring and correctness

  • Monitor latency per stage, Kafka lag, system resources.
  • Reconciliation: nightly batch recomputes from raw data and compares; mismatches alert and are corrected.

Step 4 — Wrap-up

MapReduce-style DAG over a stream, event time + watermarks, exactly-once via atomic offset commits, hotspot handling, snapshots, and reconciliation. The alternative is to buy: ClickHouse/Druid with materialized views do much of this out of the box.

.NET / Azure mapping

  • Ingestion: Event Hubs (partitioned by ad_id), capture to Data Lake for raw storage automatically.
  • Streaming aggregation: Azure Stream Analytics — SQL with TumblingWindow(minute, 1), HoppingWindow, TIMESTAMP BY clickTimestamp (event time), late-arrival and out-of-order policies built in.
  • Alternatively Azure Data Explorer with update policies / materialized views for per-minute counts, or Databricks Structured Streaming with watermarks.
  • Idempotent writes from .NET: MERGE / upsert keyed by (ad_id, minute) so replays overwrite rather than double-count.
  • Reconciliation: a scheduled Databricks / Synapse job over the lake.

Review checklist

  • Keep raw and aggregated data; raw is the source of truth.
  • Event time vs processing time; watermarks.
  • Tumbling vs sliding windows mapped to the two queries.
  • Exactly-once via atomic offset + result commit, dedupe.
  • Hotspots, snapshots, and reconciliation.
